# Temple Scroll Column 36 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 36 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 36:1 — "make places" vs. "designate places" vs. "set aside areas" — establishing quarantine zones

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall make places" | Literal 'asah — physical construction |
| LOGOS | "you shall designate places" | Administrative designation |
| PNEUMA | "set aside areas" | Dynamic, accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "you shall make places." The Hebrew 'asah implies physical construction of these quarantine areas, not merely administrative designation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 36:5 — "impurity" vs. "menstrual impurity" vs. "menstrual periods" — niddah rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in the days of their impurity" | General term, context implies menstruation |
| LOGOS | "during the days of their menstrual impurity" | Specifies the type of impurity |
| PNEUMA | "during their menstrual periods" | Modern medical terminology |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering: "in the days of their menstrual impurity." Specifying the type clarifies the verse without resorting to modern clinical language.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 36:7 — "dwell in the midst of" vs. "live among" — divine indwelling

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel" | Literal shakan betokh |
| LOGOS | "dwell in the midst of the children of Israel" | Formal, "children" for bene |
| PNEUMA | "live among the people of Israel" | Dynamic simplification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel." The Hebrew shakan betokh is theologically loaded (cf. Exodus 25:8) and should be rendered literally. "Sons of Israel" per project convention.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 36:9 — "departed from him" vs. "healed" vs. "is gone" — disease resolution

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the disease has departed from him" | Literal — disease as agent that leaves |
| LOGOS | "the disease has healed" | Medical language |
| PNEUMA | "the disease is gone" | Simple modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering: "the disease has departed from him." The Hebrew personifies the disease as departing, which is theologically significant in the Levitical skin-disease framework.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 36:14 — "make atonement" vs. "effect atonement" — kipper rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "make atonement" | Traditional rendering of kipper |
| LOGOS | "effect atonement" | Formal variant |
| PNEUMA | "make atonement" | Same as EMET |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "make atonement" per EMET and PNEUMA majority. This is the established rendering throughout the project.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/PNEUMA.

---
